title: Surgically extract aggregation micro-pools and de-bottleneck GraphQL hydration
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
The console API aggregation layer is a persistent source of p95 tail latency and memory churn during high concurrent dashboard loads. This ticket proposes a targeted refactor: extract two small aggregation micro-pools (metrics & membership) from the monolithic aggregator, introduce a lightweight hydration fastpath for GraphQL resolvers that can serve cached rollups without full resolver fanout, and simplify cache key segmentation to reduce stampedes.

Goals:
- Reduce p95 latency for dashboard and route aggregation by 25-40% under peak load.
- Cut memory churn by isolating heavy aggregation windows into bounded worker pools.
- Make cache invalidation semantics explicit for the new micro-pools to avoid stale rollups.

Approach:
1) Add two dedicated worker pools (aggregation-metrics-pool, aggregation-membership-pool) with bounded concurrency and backpressure token buckets. These will receive a pre-filtered job envelope rather than full request context.
2) Implement a GraphQL hydration fastpath that returns cached rollups for common query shapes (timeSeries + totals) and bypasses field-level fanout if the cache hit is recent and valid.
3) Replace the current monolithic cache key (route+user+window) with segmented keys that separate short-lived windows (10s) from long-lived rollups (5m). Introduce a small jitter on short windows to reduce synchronized cache evictions.
4) Add surgical integration tests and a load harness to reproduce the previous 95th/99th latency patterns.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Splitting pools increases operational surface area but lets us tune concurrency independent of the general request pool.
- Fastpath increases complexity in the resolver layer but gives a large latency reduction for the common-case dashboards; fallback to full fanout remains available.
- Jitter on cache windows may slightly reduce exactness of short-lived rollups but is acceptable for console UIs (visual smoothing).

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag the new micro-pools + fastpath.
- Canary rollout to 10% of request traffic for 48 hours with strict SLO monitoring.
- If errors or regression >10% in p99, automatically roll back the flag via the console rollout controller.

Metrics to watch:
- p50/p95/p99 latency (console-api aggregation endpoint) from Grafana dashboard
- Aggregation worker queue depth and rejection rates
- Memory RSS of aggregator pods
- Rate of cache misses/hits for short and long windows

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/aggregation-extraction-proposal
- Benchmark harness and load script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/tree/main/console-agg
- Grafana latency dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/console/aggregation-latency
- Incident learnings: https://resilience.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-01-11-console-throttle

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for new pool lifecycle and health checks.
- Integration tests to verify cache segmentation semantics and fastpath fallback correctness.
- Load test against the perf-harness to validate p95 improvement before canary.
- Chaos test: introduce synthetic latency to upstream data and ensure graceful degradation to fallback path.
